supporting: the conceptual role of pip and virtual environments

claims.claim: A Python import package is a module that can contain other modules or recursively other packages, and it provides a dotted-name hierarchy for imports.
A regular package normally has an __init__.py file; its code runs when the package is imported.
Native namespace packages can exist without __init__.py and may combine portions found in multiple directories.
A distribution package is the versioned artifact installed by an installer, while an import package is what Python imports; their names and one-to-one correspondence are not guaranteed.
A virtual environment is an isolated Python environment for a project, and pip is commonly used within it to install distribution packages.
In an import such as import garden.tools, each dotted component except the final component must be a package.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft did not distinguish the import-time meaning of package from the install-time meaning used by package managers.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced generic boilerplate with the import-package/distribution-package distinction; treated __init__.py as the normal regular-package marker rather than a universal requirement; kept installation mechanics out of scope.
